proof_review: Full approved IV Theorem 26.1.9 and II Theorem 10.7.8/Lemma 10.7.9 read and compared, including the concluding functional argument; five relevant images actually inspected.
All 27 original obligations, 19 mathematical displays, three complete solutions and the exact SVG retained. Current remote presentation edits are preserved.
Every external mathematical input has its exact current included programme proof; source access and citations to all nine books are valid.
Global positive density and half-density coefficient norms are constructed, with actual compact chart equivalence.
Every real homogeneous order uses the actual normalized Hamilton field and finite exponential lift bounds. Global escape excludes radial, zero and periodic projected curves.
B implies C uses the adjoint finite-ray realization with precisely its complete injective-cosphere hypothesis and exact forcing endpoints.
C implies B retains elliptic regularity, two-direction propagation and a complete compact limiting orbit; the limiting orbit need not avoid the forcing set.
Smooth forcing for a compact adjoint input gives smoothness, without an unsupported zero-kernel assertion.
The exhaustion incorporates all previously selected compact intervals. Last and first compact visits give minimal excursions with pairwise disjoint interiors by uniqueness.
Each realized half-ray has unattained threshold minus j; exact cutoff decomposition and locally finite supports yield one global forcing distribution.

A global candidate has one finite negative Sobolev order near K. The regularity at the other original endpoint and full forcing-regular shortened interval give the contradiction at every real operator order.
Interleaved support bounds include the justified empty initial stage and enough interior room for every later cutoff.
Uniform fixed-support continuous limits and all compact smooth forcing limits are complete; the explicit test pairing identifies their distributional equation.
Smooth completeness on an arbitrary open complement is proved with every compact chart seminorm and the full coordinate fundamental-theorem identity.
The restriction has an everywhere defined closed graph, so its every derivative estimate follows from the complete Frechet theorem.
The finite-grid estimate, countable subsequence selection, all derivative limits and chart transitions prove actual local smooth precompactness.
The normalized positive bump detectors form a countable family and separate continuous sections by explicit oscillation bounds.
Failure of the finite extension yields the correctly normalized sequence. All exterior smooth subsequential limits vanish; the full sequence therefore tends to zero.
The single compact cutoff lies in the required interior. Properness gives common output support; full all-order continuity controls every smooth remainder and the strict finite-stage contradiction.

Summable relative losses give one finite constant. The actual increasing seminorm limit has only finitely many active increments on each fixed test support, and all detector supports are locally finite.
The image map is complex-linear and its functional conjugate-linear and well-defined. Full seminorm Hahn-Banach gives the exact global extension.
The restricted functional is an actual distribution; finite-sequence density gives the bounded ell-one coefficients with their necessary conjugations.
The residual has the exact sign and is a locally finite smooth sum. The result asserts one solution modulo smooth, without a linear right inverse or exact-surjectivity claim.
The slit-domain drawing has exact affine coordinates and forward Hamilton velocity. Compact endpoints and the positive-distance argument prove the missing-origin obstruction.

All three original complete solutions remain. Two independent finite model checks cover the actual SVG coordinates and nonreal adjoint/functional conventions; they do not replace the full proof review.
